articles.article10-p1: An audit without reproducible test cases is an opinion. Test Cases A11Y turns the 87 WCAG 2.2 success criteria (levels A, AA and AAA) into a structured, bilingual catalog of executable procedures, ready to integrate into any team's QA cycle.
articles.article10-p2: Each criterion is documented in Gherkin format (Given / When / Then), the same language used by BDD tools like Cucumber. This way, an accessibility test case can be executed by a human auditor, but it can also evolve into an automatable specification without being rewritten.
articles.article10-p3: Each case states which axe-core rules partially cover it and which part demands human verification. This distinction is key: automated tools cover a fraction of WCAG, and the catalog makes explicit exactly where the boundary between automatable and manual lies for each criterion.
articles.article10-p4: The catalog includes an exporter that transforms the cases into Jira and Xray import format, so the accessibility test plan lives alongside the rest of the project's quality management instead of sitting in an isolated spreadsheet.
articles.article10-p5: All cases exist in Spanish and English, allowing international teams to audit with the same corpus and report in the client's language without improvised translations that distort WCAG's normative wording.
articles.article10-p6: The catalog is open source at github.com/ingelectronicadj/test-cases-a11y.
